panels.title: Open parties
panels.description:
Parties that exist right now.

Read from the store, so every replica reports the same value; `max` avoids adding them up.

panels.title: Players online
panels.description:
Players currently online on the network, as seen by the store.

Available from the next Quelea release; shows No data until then.

Store-backed, so `max` across replicas.

panels.title: Open event streams
panels.description:
Server-sent event streams open right now, summed over all replicas.

Every connected client holds one stream, so this is roughly the number of clients listening for party updates.

panels.title: Parties per 100 players
panels.description:
Open parties for every 100 players online.

Both inputs are store-backed and therefore taken with `max`. Divides by at least 1 so an empty network shows 0 instead of a division error.

panels.title: Parties created
panels.description: Parties created in the last 24 hours, summed over all replicas.

panels.title: Parties closed
panels.description:
Parties closed for any reason in the last 24 hours (leader disbanded, last member left, expired alone).

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Closed: expired alone
panels.description:
Parties that timed out while only their leader was still in them. Usually a sign that invites go unanswered.

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Invites sent
panels.description: Invitations that were accepted by the service (operation invite, result ok) in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Invites accepted
panels.description:
Invitations accepted in the last 24 hours (operation accept, result ok).

An accept can answer an invite sent the day before, so this is not exactly a subset of the invites above.

panels.title: Invite acceptance rate
panels.description:
Accepted invites divided by sent invites, over the last 24 hours, in percent.

Shows No data while no invite was sent, instead of a misleading 0%.

panels.title: Warps
panels.description: Party warps published in the last 24 hours (event party.warp).

panels.title: Party chat messages
panels.description: Chat messages sent inside parties in the last 24 hours (event party.chat).

panels.title: Open parties over time
panels.description:
Open parties across the time range.

Store-backed gauge: every replica reports the same value, so the series is taken with `max`, not summed.

panels.title: Parties created vs closed per hour
panels.description:
Parties opened (bars in one colour) and closed (bars in the other) in each hour.

A persistent gap between the two lines means parties accumulate.

panels.title: Closures by reason
panels.description:
Parties closed per hour, stacked by the reason they closed.

leader: the leader disbanded it. last-member-left: everyone else left. expired-alone: it timed out with only the leader in it.

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Invites sent vs accepted per hour
panels.description: Invitations sent and accepted in each hour. Accepted bars trailing sent bars is normal; a long-running gap is what to watch.

panels.title: Party lifetime (p50, p90)
panels.description:
How long a party exists from creation to closure, as a median and a 90th percentile.

A high p90 with a low p50 means most parties are short-lived and a tail is left open for a long time.

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Party lifetime by reason (p50)
panels.description:
Median lifetime, split by the reason the party closed. Parties that expire alone usually live for the full timeout; a short leader-closed median means parties are used up quickly.

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Party size after a join (last 24 hours)
panels.description:
How many joins left the party at each size, over the last 24 hours. Each join counts once, with the size the party had right after it.

Built from the cumulative histogram: each bar is the count at that size minus the count one below it.

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Average party size (24 hours)
panels.description:
Average number of members per join over the last 24 hours (sum divided by count of the size histogram).

Available from the next Quelea release.

panels.title: Operation errors per minute
panels.description:
Party operations that did not succeed, per minute, split by result code (party-full, player-not-online, lock-timeout, precondition-failed, ...). Successful operations are excluded.

A rising line for one code points at that failure; a spike across many codes usually means a broken client or an outage.

panels.title: HTTP requests by status
panels.description:
Requests per second handled by the HTTP server, split by status code.

A 5xx line is a server fault; a 4xx line usually means clients sending requests the API rejects.

panels.title: Lock timeouts per minute
panels.description: Operations that gave up waiting for a party lock (result lock-timeout). Parties are locked while they are changed, so this rises under contention or when a request hangs.

panels.title: Precondition failures per minute
panels.description: Operations rejected because the party state did not match what the caller expected (result precondition-failed). Mostly stale clients acting on an old view of a party.

panels.title: Average HTTP latency
panels.description:
Mean time per HTTP request over the last few minutes (sum of durations divided by count). A mean hides tail latency, so read it with the request rate above.

Uses count and sum only, so it works even where the histogram buckets are missing.

panels.title: Open event streams over time
panels.description: Server-sent event streams open over time, summed over all replicas. A step down that does not match a deploy suggests clients are dropping.

panels.title: Stream overflow disconnects per minute
panels.description: Event streams the service closed because a client could not keep up (reason overflow). The client then has to reconnect and may miss events.

panels.title: Failed event publishes per minute
panels.description: Party events that could not be published, per minute, split by event type. Failed events are not retried, so clients may not see the change until they refresh.
